newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebels push west, say they capture Kindu.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels push west, say they capture Kindu.

text.p: Zairean rebels said they captured the large town of Kindu, pushing westwards the expanding area they control in eastern Zaire.
Jean Kabongo, special security adviser to rebel leader Laurent Kabila, told Reuters in Goma on Tuesday night: "We have Kindu, Bunia and Walikale, as well as Butembo and Lubero."

Kindu, about 320 km (200 miles) west of Zaire's eastern borders, is the most westerly town the rebels say they have captured. It is on the Zaire River, upstream from the city of Kisangani, the rebels' next big target.

Commander Kabongo said: "Kisangani is surrounded, but we haven't moved in yet. When we do, we will be in a position to travel down the river to Kinshasa. This fighting has been hard for our troops, but they are used to it, they are from here."
The rebels started in October with the towns of Goma and Bukavu on the Rwandan border. They now hold towns along a front 550 km (340 miles) long and running north-south.
